Hi Sandeep / Dana —

Following up on our call about the November maintenance window for your private VPC deployment. We want to propose a short, tightly scoped maintenance plan focused on safe version stewardship (pinning/unpinning) and an explicit emergency-unpin path if a post-upgrade regression is detected. High level: 

- Proposed window (pick one):
  - Tue Nov 26, 02:00–05:00 PT (low traffic)
  - Wed Nov 27, 22:00–01:00 PT (alternate)
- Scope: minor runtime patch + model runtime lib bump (non-breaking), two-stage canary (10% then 100%), KV-cache warmup and validation.
- Safety controls: automatic rollback on error-rate > 2x baseline OR token-generation latency > 150ms for 5 consecutive minutes.
- Emergency unpin flow: immediate unpin to prior version via Ops console + targeted instance evacuation (per-rack) — full checklist attached.

Attachments: acme_maint_window_proposal.pdf (timeline + blackout map) and private-emergency-unpin-checklist.md (runbook). Please review the attachments; we specifically need:
  1) confirmation of preferred window by EOD Mon Nov 18;
  2) network contact on your side who can coordinate BGP/flavor changes if we need to shift traffic between regions;
  3) approval to run a small safety injection (synthetic traffic tests) 30 minutes before canary.

Notes on networking: our plan assumes no customer-side firewall rules will block health-checks from Redwood NAT IPs (listed in the PDF). If you have strict egress filtering, please share the ACL owner so we can pre-authorize.

Next steps if we get confirmation: Karthik will publish a minute-by-minute runbook and we’ll create a DocuSign approval packet for your legal sign-off.

Thanks —

Hi all — answering the KV/cache question and adding operational detail. TL;DR: we avoid mass session invalidation during unpin by performing a staged evacuation + KV-prefill and targeted network drain. Details below.

Plan (short):
1) Canary (10%) — serve traffic against new version with KV-warmup enabled. Validate synthetic probes and real-traffic metrics for 20 minutes.
2) Ramp (100%) — if canary passes, move remaining traffic. If canary fails, we automatically re-route the canary subset back to the pinned version and execute the emergency-unpin checklist only for canary hosts (no global unpin).
3) Emergency global unpin (only on explicit approval or severe metric triggers):
   - Mark pinned version in the control plane as "evacuate-now" (atomic flag).
   - For each cluster/rack: perform graceful drain (60s grace) on serving instances, start prior-version tasks, prefill KV from cold snapshot, then promote traffic. This avoids token/session churn in most cases.
   - If a host is forcibly terminated before prefill completes, impacted sessions will see short-lived 5xx and application-level retries are required. We recommend our customer apps have a 2s jittered retry on 5xx and idempotency on prompt submissions.

Operational safeguards we will run (all included in the checklist): preflight health probes, SST run, BGP failover test in staging, and a post-traffic audit with request-sampling. Priyom will coordinate the DocuSign and the runbook updates.

Karthik
